documents.summary: Protocols from ASIS, Cooper's Color Code, and UK Police for when followed on foot
documents.guidance:
If you suspect someone is following you on foot:
1. **Verify Without Confronting (Cooper's Code Orange):** Make 4 consecutive right turns around a block or cross diagonally. If the individual replicates your path, pursuit is confirmed.
2. **Change Speed & Environmental Lighting:** Alter your pace suddenly. Move toward illuminated, high-traffic venues (supermarkets, petrol stations, hotel lobbies, ATM kiosks with security guards).
3. **Never Lead Pursuers Home:** Do not retreat to your residence or enter dead-end alleys where you can be cornered.
4. **Discreetly Arm SilentSOS:** Open SilentSOS and enable **Stealth Mode** so live GPS telemetry, dual camera bursts, and ambient audio stream to your emergency contacts.
5. **Assertive Verbal Boundary:** If the pursuer closes distance, pivot with hands in a defensive frame, make firm eye contact, and shout loudly: *'Stop! Back away! My live GPS tracking is alerting emergency response!'*
6. **Contact Emergency Services:** Dial **112 (India/EU)** or **911 (US)** immediately.

documents.summary: Instinctive defense and release mechanics from Krav Maga and Gracie Survival Tactics
documents.guidance:
If an aggressor attacks physically and evasion is impossible:
1. **Target Soft Vulnerable Anatomy:** Strike decisively to create an immediate opening to flee:
• **Eyes:** Palm-thrust or gouge to trigger involuntary ocular defense and head retraction.
• **Throat / Trachea:** Open palm-heel strike disrupts respiration and induces coughing spasms.
• **Groin:** Upward knee drive or snappy heel kick collapses posture.
• **Shin / Instep:** Stomp downward onto the attacker's arch or scrape the shin bone with shoe edge.
2. **Escaping Wrist Seizures:** Rotate your wrist toward the attacker's thumb (the weakest structural point of any grip) while stepping backward.
3. **Escaping Rear Chokeholds / Bear Hugs:** Drop your center of gravity rapidly. Deliver backward headbutts to their nose, drive elbows into the solar plexus, and stomp their instep.
4. **Disengage and Sprint:** Do not grapple or stay to fight once an opening is created. Run toward public visibility while yelling *'FIRE!'* or *'HELP! CALL 112/911!'*

documents.summary: Adult Hands-Only CPR according to AHA, ERC, and ILCOR protocols
documents.guidance:
If a person collapses, is unresponsive, and is not breathing normally:
1. **Call 112 / 911 / 999:** Place phone on speaker so dispatchers can assist you while you work.
2. **Firm Hard Surface:** Position the victim flat on their back on a solid floor.
3. **Hand Placement:** Position the heel of your dominant hand in the center of the chest (lower half of breastbone). Interlock your other hand on top. Lock elbows straight.
4. **Compress Hard and Fast:**
• Push down at least **2 inches (5 cm)**.
• Maintain a rate of **100 to 120 compressions per minute** (the tempo of *'Stayin\' Alive'*).
• Allow full chest recoil between every thrust without leaning.
5. **Continuous Compressions:** Do not stop hands-only compressions until emergency paramedics arrive or an Automated External Defibrillator (AED) is attached and prompts you to stand clear.

documents.summary: Trauma hemorrhage management from Stop The Bleed and St John Ambulance
documents.guidance:
For life-threatening or spurting bleeding:
1. **Direct Firm Pressure:** Place clean cloth or sterile gauze over the wound. Press down with both hands using your full upper body weight.
2. **Never Remove Blood-Soaked Cloths:** If blood soaks through, add additional layers directly on top. Removing dressings tears away developing platelet clots.
3. **Wound Packing (Groin, Armpits, Neck Base):** Tightly pack cloth into deep cavity wounds until full, then apply unrelenting direct pressure.
4. **Tourniquet Application (Limbs Only):**
• For uncontrolled bleeding on arms or legs, apply a tourniquet **2 to 3 inches above the wound** (closer to the torso, never over a joint).
• Tighten until all bleeding ceases and distal pulse vanishes. Note the exact application time.
5. **Prevent Hypothermic Shock:** Keep the casualty warm with blankets or coats and lay them flat.

documents.summary: Heimlich maneuver and self-rescue from AHA and Mayo Clinic
documents.guidance:
If a person cannot speak, cough, or breathe and is clutching their throat (universal choking sign):
1. **Conscious Adult Protocol:**
• Stand behind victim, wrap your arms around their waist.
• Make a fist with one hand; place thumb side slightly above the navel (below ribcage).
• Grasp fist with other hand and deliver quick, forceful **upward and inward abdominal thrusts**.
• Repeat until the obstruction pops out or the patient loses consciousness.
2. **Self-Heimlich When Alone:**
• Position your own fist above navel, lean over the back of a rigid chair, table rim, or balcony rail, and drive abdomen sharply into the edge.
3. **If Victim Collapses:** Lower them carefully to the ground, call 112 / 911, and begin chest compressions immediately.

documents.summary: DHS / CISA Run-Hide-Fight protocol for active hostile events
documents.guidance:
During an active hostility or shooting incident:
1. **RUN (Primary Objective):** If an accessible escape path exists, evacuate immediately regardless of whether others agree to follow. Leave belongings behind. Keep hands visible for law enforcement.
2. **HIDE (If Escape is Blocked):**
• Find a secure room. Lock and barricade doors with heavy desks, vending machines, or wedges.
• Turn off lights, silence cellphones (turn off vibrations), and stay low away from windows.
• Arm SilentSOS in **Stealth Mode** to silently beacon your GPS and audio to responders.
3. **FIGHT (Absolute Last Resort):** If your life is in imminent peril, act aggressively: commit to disarming the threat, throw heavy items (fire extinguishers, chairs), work together with others, and incapacitate the attacker.

documents.summary: USGS & NDMA Earthquake survival guidelines
documents.guidance:
When the ground shakes during an earthquake:
1. **DROP:** Drop down onto your hands and knees. This position protects you from being knocked down and allows crawling to shelter.
2. **COVER:** Take cover under a sturdy desk or table. Protect your head and neck with your arms. If no shelter is nearby, crawl next to an interior wall away from glass windows and heavy hanging mirrors.
3. **HOLD ON:** Hold onto your shelter with one hand and protect head/neck with the other until shaking stops.
4. **If Indoors:** Stay inside! Running outside during shaking is when most falling brick and glass injuries occur.
5. **After Shaking Stops:** Check for gas leaks, evacuate carefully via stairs (never use elevators), and check in via SilentSOS.

In situations of domestic coercion, violence, or escalating threats:
1. **Pack a Secret Evacuation Kit:** Stash cash, copies of identification, passports, prescriptions, deeds, duplicate house/car keys, and a secondary charger with a trusted friend or neighbor.
2. **Avoid Physical Traps:** In escalating arguments, stay out of rooms with hard surfaces or weapons (kitchens with knives, bathrooms with slippery tile floors).
3. **Use SilentSOS Covert Tools:**
• **Fake Call Simulator:** Triggers an authentic incoming phone call from 'Mom' to create a natural, urgent excuse to leave the premises.
• **Stealth Mode:** Appears as an inert, blacked-out screen while secretly recording ambient threats and streaming live coordinates to trusted guardians.
4. **Emergency Helplines (Confidential):**
• India: Women in Distress **1091** or **181** | Unified Police **112**
• US: National Domestic Violence Hotline **1-800-799-7233** or text **START to 88788**
• UK: National Domestic Abuse Helpline **0808 2000 247**

documents.summary: Detecting spyware and securing mobile devices from EFF, CISA, and Coalition Against Stalkerware
documents.guidance:
If you suspect your phone is being monitored by an abuser or stalker:
1. **Warning Indicators:** Unexpected rapid battery drain, device overheating when idle, spikes in mobile data usage, or unfamiliar apps in Device Admin / Accessibility services.
2. **Check App Permissions:** Audit which applications have access to Location ('Allow all the time'), Camera, and Microphone. Revoke suspicious permissions.
3. **Do Not Immediately Delete Spyware:** If safe, consult domestic violence specialists or police first—deleting stalkerware can alert an abuser that they have been discovered.
4. **Use a Secondary Clean Device:** Use a library computer or a friend's phone for sensitive searches, safety planning, and communicating with advocates.
5. **Harden Screen Lock:** Use a fresh 6-digit alphanumeric passcode that the abuser cannot guess. Disable biometric unlock if coerced fingerprint access is a risk.

documents.summary: Zero FIR rights and cryptographic digital evidence preservation from Supreme Court of India and CPS
documents.guidance:
Your constitutional legal rights when reporting crime and preserving evidence:
1. **Zero FIR Mandate (India):** Under Supreme Court precedent (Lalita Kumari vs. Govt of UP), any police station is legally required to register a First Information Report (FIR) for cognizable offences regardless of where the incident occurred. Refusal is an offence under Section 166A IPC / BNSS.
2. **Right to Female Police Officer:** Female victims have the statutory right to have their statement recorded by a woman police officer or magistrate.
3. **Evidentiary Integrity in SilentSOS:**
• Photos, audio recordings, and GPS breadcrumbs stored in the SilentSOS Evidence Vault contain embedded UTC timestamps and cryptographic checksums.
• Do not crop, edit, or filter files prior to police submission to maintain unbroken chain of custody in court proceedings.

documents.summary: Vehicle safety, child locks, and route anomalies from NHTSA, Uber, and TfL
documents.guidance:
Precautionary steps when taking cabs or rideshares:
1. **Pre-Boarding Verification:** Always ask the driver: *'Who are you here to pick up?'* Let them say your name first. Match the license plate and driver photo precisely.
2. **Back Seat Seating:** Sit on the rear passenger side. This provides maximum reaction distance and prevents the driver from easily reaching you.
3. **Test the Door & Child Lock:** Check that the interior door handle works immediately upon sitting. If the child lock is active and the door cannot open from inside, demand to exit immediately.
4. **Share Live Trip Breadcrumbs:** Share your SilentSOS tracking link with emergency contacts so they can see your real-time GPS location.
5. **In Case of Route Deviation or Threat:**
• Speak up firmly: *'You have turned off the GPS route. Stop the vehicle right now.'*
• Trigger SilentSOS covertly using the shake accelerometer or physical volume keys.
• If the car slows at an intersection or traffic signal, unlock the door, exit into traffic, and shout for assistance.

documents.summary: Grounding and panic de-escalation protocols from SAMHSA, NAMI, and Mind
documents.guidance:
If you or someone nearby is experiencing acute panic, hyperventilation, or extreme terror:
1. **The 5-4-3-2-1 Sensory Grounding Technique:** Name aloud:
• **5 things you can SEE** (e.g. wall clock, shoes, tree, doorknob, street lamp)
• **4 things you can physically FEEL** (e.g. feet on the floor, texture of clothing, cool phone case, chair back)
• **3 things you can HEAR** (e.g. distant cars, breathing, air conditioning)
• **2 things you can SMELL** (e.g. rain, coffee, clothing soap)
• **1 thing you can TASTE** (or say: *'I am safe right now in this exact moment'*)
2. **4-4-4-4 Box Breathing:**
• Inhale slowly through nose for **4 seconds**
• Hold breath gently for **4 seconds**
• Exhale smoothly through mouth for **4 seconds**
• Hold lungs empty for **4 seconds**
• Repeat 4 times to stimulate the parasympathetic nervous system and slow heart rate.
3. **Confidential Crisis Lines:** Text **HOME to 741741** (US/UK) or dial **14416** (Tele-MANAS India) / **988** (US).

documents.guidance:
🔒 **SilentSOS Safety PIN Security Protocol:**

• **Default Factory PIN:** Initialized as **`1234`** across all installations.
• **Anti-Tamper Lockout:** Once an emergency SOS beacon or distress trigger is armed, it CANNOT be cancelled, muted, or deleted without entering this 4-digit PIN. This prevents an aggressor from coercing you into turning off your distress alert.
• **How to Change PIN:**
1. Web App: Navigate to **Settings → Security & PIN → Change PIN**. Enter your current PIN (`1234` by default), then type your new 4-digit code and confirm.
2. Android App: Navigate to **Settings tab → Change Safety PIN**, enter your new 4 digits, and tap Save.
• **Recommendation:** Change the PIN from `1234` immediately upon initial onboarding.

4. **Hand Gesture Computer Vision (Web & Mobile):** Open the **Gestures** tab and raise an open flat palm toward the camera for contactless optical arming.
5. **Category Distress Buttons:** Direct tap on **Police**, **Fire**, **Medical**, or **Personal Threat** for specialized priority triage.

documents.summary: Legal rights during reporting, Zero FIR rules, and digital evidence preservation
documents.guidance:
⚖️ **Legal Rights & Evidence Preservation Protocol:**

1. **Zero FIR Right (India):** You have the legal right to lodge an FIR at ANY police station, regardless of jurisdiction or where the incident occurred. The police station cannot turn you away; they must register a 'Zero FIR' and transfer it to the relevant jurisdictional station.
2. **Right to Female Officer:** A woman has the right to record her statement before a female police officer or magistrate (under Section 154 CrPC / BNSS).
3. **Preserving Digital Evidence:**
• Do not edit, crop, or apply filters to photos or audio captured in the SilentSOS Evidence Vault.
• The cryptographic timestamp, GPS geolocation tags, and camera hashes stored in SilentSOS establish evidentiary integrity and admissible chain of custody.
• Export incident summaries and audio files to secure cloud backup before handing devices to authorities.

documents.summary: Step-by-step adult Hands-Only CPR instructions
documents.guidance:
If a person collapses, is unresponsive, and is not breathing or only gasping:
1. **Call Emergency Services First:** Dial **112 / 911 / 999** immediately and put the phone on speaker.
2. **Position the Patient:** Lay the person flat on their back on a firm, hard surface.
3. **Hand Placement:** Place the heel of one hand in the center of the person's chest (between the nipples). Interlock your other hand on top, keeping elbows locked straight.
4. **Compress Hard and Fast:**
• Push down at least **2 inches (5 cm)** deep.
• Maintain a rhythm of **100 to 120 beats per minute** (match the tempo of the song *'Stayin' Alive'*).
• Allow the chest to recoil completely between compressions.
5. **Do NOT Stop:** Continue hands-only compressions without interruption until emergency medical paramedics arrive or an Automated External Defibrillator (AED) is attached.

documents.summary: Controlling severe life-threatening bleeding and hemorrhage
documents.guidance:
For severe or spurting blood loss:
1. **Direct Firm Pressure:** Immediately place a sterile gauze, clean cloth, or clothing over the wound. Press down with both hands using your full body weight.
2. **Do Not Remove Saturated Cloths:** If blood soaks through, add more layers on top and press harder. Removing the first cloth tears away forming clots.
3. **Wound Packing:** For deep junctional wounds (groin, armpit, neck base), pack cloth tightly directly into the wound cavity, then apply heavy pressure.
4. **Tourniquet Application (Limbs Only):**
• If bleeding from an arm or leg is arterial/uncontrolled, apply a commercial or improvised tourniquet **2 to 3 inches above the wound** (closer to the torso, not over a joint).
• Tighten until bleeding completely stops and the pulse below is gone.
• Note down the exact time of application.
5. **Prevent Shock:** Keep the patient lying flat, elevate legs slightly if possible, and cover with a jacket/blanket to preserve body temperature.

documents.summary: First aid for thermal and scald burns
documents.guidance:
For thermal burns from fire, hot liquids, or hot objects:
1. **Cool Immediately with Water:** Run cool (not freezing or ice-cold) tap water over the burn for at least **10 to 20 minutes**.
2. **Do NOT Use Ice, Butter, or Toothpaste:** Ice causes further tissue death (frostbite injury); butter and oils trap heat and encourage bacterial infection.
3. **Remove Constricting Items:** Gently take off rings, watches, belts, or tight clothing around the burn before swelling begins.
4. **Cover Cleanly:** Cover loosely with sterile non-stick dressing or clean cling film.
5. **Seek Emergency Care If:** The burn is larger than the palm of your hand, causes white/charred skin, or is on the face, hands, joints, or groin.

documents.summary: Tactical protocol when someone is following you on foot
documents.guidance:
If you suspect you are being followed on foot:
1. **Confirm Without Confronting:** Make 3 or 4 right turns to circle a block. If they follow, your suspicion is confirmed. Cross the street diagonally.
2. **Change Speed & Direction:** Suddenly change pace or duck into an open, well-lit business (café, pharmacy, supermarket, bank with ATM guards).
3. **Do NOT Go Home or Down Dark Alleys:** Never lead a pursuer to your doorstep or isolated alleys where you could be trapped.
4. **Discreetly Arm SilentSOS:** Open SilentSOS and hold your finger on the SOS button, or enable **Stealth Mode** so live GPS breadcrumbs and audio recording stream to your contacts.
5. **Create Public Awareness:** If they close the distance, turn firmly with hands up in a defensive barrier, make eye contact, and speak loudly: *'Stay back! I am on live emergency tracking with police!'*
6. **Call Emergency Services:** Immediately dial 112 (India/EU) or 911 (US) and describe your exact intersection, clothing, and the suspect's appearance.

documents.summary: Safety precautions and crisis response in taxis and rideshares
documents.guidance:
When taking a cab or rideshare:
1. **Pre-Boarding Verification:** Always confirm the driver says YOUR name first (*'Who are you here for?'*), match the vehicle license plate, and inspect the driver photo.
2. **Sit in the Back Seat:** Never sit in the front passenger seat. Sitting on the rear passenger side maximizes reaction distance and lets you see the driver.
3. **Check Child Locks:** Open and close the rear door slightly from the inside before leaving to ensure the inside handle functions and child-safety locks are not engaged.
4. **Share Live Tracking:** Share your live SilentSOS GPS link or trip route with trusted guardians before entering the vehicle.
5. **If Driver Deviates or Refuses to Stop:**
• Speak up firmly: *'You have deviated from the GPS route. Stop here immediately.'*
• Trigger SilentSOS covertly using volume button/shake gestures.
• If held against your will at a red light or slow traffic, roll down the window, scream for help, unlock the door and exit immediately into a crowd.

documents.summary: Survival guidelines during a home invasion or burglary
documents.guidance:
If you hear an intruder or suspect someone has broken into your home:
1. **Do NOT Search the House:** Never confront an intruder. Your goal is survival, not protecting property.
2. **Shelter in Place (Safe Room):** Retreat to a room with a lockable solid door (bathroom or bedroom). Lock the door and barricade it with heavy furniture.
3. **Silent Distress:** Keep the lights OFF. Do not make noise. Activate SilentSOS in Stealth Mode to transmit your GPS, live audio, and emergency email notification without alerting the intruder.
4. **Call Emergency Responders:** Whisper to 112 / 911 dispatch. State: *'Intruder in my house at [Your Address]. I am barricaded in the second-floor bedroom. Send armed police immediately.'*
5. **Prepare Defense Weapon:** If the barricade fails, grab an improvised impact tool (heavy flashlight, fire extinguisher, chair) and aim for vulnerable areas (face, throat, groin).

documents.summary: Discreet safety planning and emergency exit for domestic violence situations
documents.guidance:
In situations involving an aggressive or abusive household:
1. **Secret Evacuation Bag:** Prepare a hidden emergency kit with cash, copies of identification, bank cards, essential medicines, duplicate keys, and a backup charger.
2. **Avoid Enclosed Traps:** In escalating conflicts, avoid rooms with no exit or easy access to weapons (kitchens with knives, bathrooms with slippery tile surfaces).
3. **Use SilentSOS Disguises:**
• Use **Fake Call Simulator** to create an immediate plausible reason to step out (*'My boss is calling, I have to step outside'*).
• Keep **Stealth Mode** configured so the screen appears off even if you activate distress.
4. **Emergency Safe Word:** Establish a code word with trusted contacts or neighbors (*'Can you lend me a recipe book?'*) that signals them to call the police.
5. **National Helplines:** Reach out confidentially:
• India: Women Helpline **1091** or **181** | Police **112**
• US: National Domestic Violence Hotline **1-800-799-SAFE (7233)**
• UK: National Helpline **0808 2000 247**

documents.summary: Core physical self-defense principles against an attacker
documents.guidance:
If physically attacked and escape is impossible:
1. **Target Soft Vulnerable Points:** Attackers do not expect decisive counters. Target:
• **Eyes:** Gouge or strike to cause immediate blinding and reflexive head pull-back.
• **Throat/Windpipe:** Open-hand palm strike creates airway disruption.
• **Groin:** Knee strike or upward kick causes sudden collapse.
• **Shin/Instep:** Stomp your heel downward onto the attacker's foot or scrape the shin.
2. **Breaking a Wrist Grip:** Rotate your wrist toward the attacker's thumb (the weakest point of the grip) and yank your arm back sharply while stepping back.
3. **If Grabbed from Behind:** Drive your heel down onto their instep, strike backward with an elbow into their solar plexus or chin, and twist your hips to create space.
4. **Sprint and Shout:** Never stay to continue fighting once you create an opening. Run immediately toward crowds while yelling specific commands (*'FIRE!'* or *'HELP! CALL POLICE!'*).

documents.summary: Stealth Mode disguise and covert background tracking
documents.guidance:
🕶️ **SilentSOS Stealth Mode & Covert Defense:**

• **What It Does:** Renders a completely blank, dark, simulated 'power-off' screen across your device so observers or hostile individuals cannot see that an emergency app is running.
• **Background Engine:** Even with the black screen active, SilentSOS continues running high-precision GPS tracking, dual photographic bursts, ambient microphone capture, and automatic cloud/email dispatches.
• **How to Toggle On/Off:**
1. In Web App: Go to **Settings → Stealth & Disguise → Stealth Mode toggle**.
2. In Android App: Go to **Settings tab → Stealth Mode switch**, or activate directly from the SOS Hub.
• **Tactical Recommendation:** Keep Stealth Mode armed whenever traveling late at night, walking alone in unlit areas, or when in high-risk transit.

documents.summary: Safety PIN security and alert cancellation protocol
documents.guidance:
🔒 **SilentSOS Safety PIN Security Protocol:**

• **Default Master PIN:** Every new account and fresh install is initialized with default PIN **1234**.
• **Purpose of Safety PIN:** Once an SOS beacon or distress trigger is armed, it CANNOT be cancelled or muted without entering this 4-digit code. This prevents an aggressor or coerced phone inspection from silencing your distress call.
• **How to Change PIN:**
1. In Web App: Navigate to **Settings → Security & PIN → Change PIN**. Type your current PIN (`1234` by default), followed by your new 4-digit code, and confirm.
2. In Android Native App: Navigate to **Settings tab → Change Safety PIN**, enter your new 4 digits, and tap Save.
• **Security Best Practice:** Change the default PIN immediately after initial setup to a memorized sequence unknown to anyone else.

documents.summary: Fake Call Simulator for covert tactical withdrawal
documents.guidance:
📞 **Fake Call Escape Simulator:**

• **Purpose:** Simulates an ultra-realistic incoming phone call (displaying 'Mom' with ringing and haptic vibration) to give you an immediate, unsuspicious excuse to walk away from uncomfortable, threatening, or suspicious company.
• **How to Launch:**
1. On Web App: Open **Settings → Fake Call Disguise → Test**.
2. On Android App: Open **Settings tab → Fake Call Escape Simulator**.
• **Tactical Usage:** Answer the call, hold phone to ear, pretend to speak (*'Yes, I\'m on my way right now, I\'m 2 minutes away'*), and briskly walk toward a well-populated, lit area.

documents.summary: All 5 methods to trigger the SilentSOS emergency distress beacon
documents.guidance:
🚨 **5 Multi-Vector SOS Emergency Triggers:**

1. **3-Second Press & Hold (Web & Android):** Press and hold the glowing central SOS button on the Hub. A 3-second haptic countdown begins before arming distress.
2. **Mobile Accelerometer Shake (Android):** Violently shake your mobile phone back and forth 3 times. The accelerometer detects sudden high-g spikes and arms distress without needing to unlock the screen.
3. **Hardware Volume Key Sequence (Android):** Press physical Volume Up or Volume Down keys in rapid succession.
4. **Hand Gesture Computer Vision (Web & Mobile):** Open the **Gestures** tab and raise an open flat palm toward the camera for contactless optical arming.
5. **Category Distress Buttons:** Direct tap on **Police**, **Fire**, **Medical**, or **Personal Threat** for specialized priority triage.

documents.summary: Autonomous photo burst, audio recording, video buffer, and Evidence Vault viewer
documents.guidance:
🛡️ **SilentSOS Autonomous Multi-Media Evidence Vault:**

• **Automated Dual-Camera Bursts:** When SOS triggers, the device takes rapid front and rear photo bursts stamped with UTC timestamps, GPS coordinates, and cryptographic hashes.
• **High-Fidelity Audio Buffer:** Automatically records surrounding ambient audio through the microphone to capture threats, perpetrator voices, and vehicular sounds.
• **Rolling Video Container:** Captures streaming video evidence without screen flashes.
• **In-App Vault Viewer:** Tap the **Evidence** tab on Web or Android to review all historical incident sessions, browse photo galleries, play audio files, and inspect GPS telemetry.
• **Cloud & Email Dispatch:** All evidence media is packaged and securely dispatched to your emergency contacts via Resend.

documents.summary: Managing emergency guardians and automated Resend alert dispatch
documents.guidance:
👥 **Emergency Contacts & Automated Dispatch Pipeline:**

• **Adding Contacts:** Go to the **Contacts** tab, click **Add Guardian**, and specify their full name, phone number, relationship, and email address.
• **Live Dispatch Content:** When distress activates, each contact receives:
1. Instant SMS with direct Google Maps link.
2. Formal Resend Email containing live coordinates, medical information, and links to all captured photos/audio.
• **Testing Resend Delivery:** In **Settings → Resend Alert Notifications**, click **Send Test Alert Notification** to verify your contacts' inboxes receive the alert successfully.
